purpose: FR-20 named behavior-preservation baseline for the Conversations Boilerplate Reduction initiative (Story 1.1). This is the trusted, unchanging behavioral reference that every later refactor (Epics 2-5) diffs against. It records the conformance oracle proven green on unmodified main, the public-contract-shape snapshot pointer, and the oracle survivability classification handed off to Story 1.3.
workingTreeState: src/ and tests/ clean at capture time (no local edits to production or test sources)

suiteClasses.releaseGateBehavior: adopter integration surface (tenant binding, idempotency, projection freshness, compatibility, error envelope)

projectTotalAtBaseline.note: Full Hexalith.Conversations.Conformance.Tests project run on unmodified main (commit ceb7fbe), before Story 1.1 added the test-only PublicContractShapeSnapshotGenerationTest. The 248 total = the 214 suite-class tests + 34 tests across the 4 non-suite validation classes (ConformanceManifestValidationTest, CoreFixtureContentSafetyTest, ReleaseConformanceArtifactGenerationTest, ReleaseWaiverValidationTest).

publicContractShapeSnapshot.note: Deterministic reflection snapshot of the exported public contract surface. Closed vocabularies (e.g. ConversationErrorCode) use the Hexalith smart-enum record pattern, captured as static properties rather than CLR enum members.

oracleSurvivability.description: AC3 classification of each conformance suite as public-surface-only (depends only on Hexalith.Conversations.Contracts/.Client/.Testing public types, HTTP, or DomainResult) or internally-coupled (depends on Hexalith.Conversations.Server.* plumbing types or internal/reflection access). Verified by inspecting using-directives and instantiated types of each suite test class AND its companion engine/fixture files. Classification only - nothing was decoupled in Story 1.1.

internallyCoupled.coupling: using Hexalith.Conversations.Server.Diagnostics and Hexalith.Conversations.Server.TenantAccess; instantiates server-internal types ConversationCommandRejectionClass and ConversationTenantDenialClass and the server-side TelemetryCardinalityConformanceSuite engine.

using Hexalith.Conversations.Server.Diagnostics and Hexalith.Conversations.Server.TenantAccess; instantiates ConversationCommandRejectionClass / ConversationTenantDenialClass and the server-side TelemetryRedactionConformanceSuite engine.

The test class itself only uses Hexalith.Conversations.Testing.Fixtures, BUT its companion engine ConformanceStatusConformanceSuite.cs and fixtures ConformanceStatusConformanceFixtures.cs depend on Hexalith.Conversations.Server.Diagnostics, binding to the server-internal types ConversationConformanceStatusClassifier and ConversationConformanceStatusClass.
internallyCoupled.discrepancyNote: DISCREPANCY: Story 1.1's pre-analysis table classified this suite (#7) as public-surface-only. Verification per AC3 ('verify, do not trust it blindly') found it is internally coupled through its engine/fixtures. Recorded here and flagged to Story 1.3.

alsoCoupledSupportFile.coupling: Shared fixture (not one of the 14 suite test classes) that also depends on Hexalith.Conversations.Server.Diagnostics / Server.TenantAccess (ConversationCommandRejectionClass, ConversationTenantDenialClass). Noted for completeness so Story 1.3 does not miss it when decoupling.

projectLevelCoupling.risk: References Hexalith.Conversations.Server (in addition to Contracts, Client, Testing). This project-level reference is the structural reason the telemetry/conformance-status suites can compile against Server.Diagnostics. For a fully refactor-survivable oracle the public-surface suites must not transitively depend on the plumbing assembly being refactored.
projectLevelCoupling.action: Recorded as a survivability risk for Story 1.3 triage. Deliberately NOT removed in Story 1.1 (removing it would break the coupled suites' compilation, which is Story 1.3's job to resolve).

oracleSurvivability.handoffTo: Story 1.3 (decouple the internally-coupled tests that would break under refactor)
